title: arXiv Physics — 14 October 2026 batch: eight notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official popularity ranking; this is an inferred selection based on checkable scientific signals, not a readership or download chart. The papers were just announced, so citation data are too sparse to establish momentum.

sections.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
sections.abstract: The authors use a graphene quantum Hall dot to trap and tune down to a single fractional quasiparticle, and report charge-addition patterns consistent with an anyon-binding energy comparable to the charging energy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report resonances consistent with e/3 charge transport and suppression of alternating charge sectors, interpreted as attractive inter-anyon interactions and an anyon binding energy at least as large as the charging energy.
sections.unique_caveat: The binding interpretation combines transport/charge-addition signatures with modeling; large-quasiparticle-number wavefunctions are not known precisely. This is not a direct braiding-statistics measurement.

sections.title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
sections.abstract: The authors prepare and characterize W, GHZ, and cluster states in mechanical resonator modes, certify genuine multipartite entanglement among as many as four modes, and use the states to bound collective dephasing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use optimal-control pulses between a superconducting transmon and successive modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator to prepare bond-dimension-two matrix-product states, certifying genuine multipartite entanglement through four modes.
sections.unique_caveat: Certification is currently limited to four modes; decoherence, preparation errors, and sequential tomography duration limit scaling.

sections.title: A Spatial Map of the Atmospheric Limb of a Hot Jupiter
sections.abstract: Applying transmission-string mapping to JWST observations of WASP-17b, the authors resolve temperature variation around the planet's transmitting limb and report an approximately 650 K morning–evening contrast.
sections.claimed_result: The authors map WASP-17b from 0.6–12 μm using JWST NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI data, finding a hotter evening limb and constraining H2O and CO2 abundances around the limb.
sections.unique_caveat: This is one planet, and the morning-side temperature has broad uncertainties (858 K with +434/−233 K); independent coverage notes a north–south symmetry assumption.

sections.title: The 3He(α,γ)7Be γ-ray angular distribution: measured, and calculated by effective field theory
sections.abstract: The authors report the first comprehensive angular distribution measurement for this astrophysically important reaction, using 22 high-purity germanium detectors and comparing the data with an EFT-based calculation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measured γ-ray angular distributions from 27° to 145° over 442–1213 keV center-of-mass energies; they report agreement with a hybrid EFT treatment when E1, M1, and E2 interference is included.
sections.unique_caveat: The activation method contributes only one S-factor point; broader extrapolation beyond the measured angular data depends on the reaction model.

sections.title: Evidence for Distinct One-Off and Repeating Subpopulations in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2
sections.abstract: Using simulation-based inference on CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, the authors find that models with a truly one-off FRB subpopulation fit better than single-population alternatives, with a random-forest analysis as a second check.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the catalog favors models containing a one-off population and predict the repeater fraction will fall below 2% within five years, eventually reaching about 0.5% as the catalog saturates.
sections.unique_caveat: This is population-model inference, not a direct identification of intrinsically non-repeating individual sources; predictions remain to be tested against later catalogs.

sections.title: Energy, vertex, and time response of a LiquidO detector with an opaque-scintillator target to Compton-tagged electrons
sections.abstract: A 4-liter LiquidO prototype was calibrated with Compton-tagged electrons; the collaboration reports a linear light yield, energy resolution, position localization, and a lower bound on start-time response.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports 48.3 ± 1.5 photoelectrons/MeV across four operating points, (23.4 ± 0.4)% energy resolution, localization bounded by the 20 mm beam spot, and a ≥1.5 ns lower bound on single-scatter start time.
sections.unique_caveat: The results are prototype-scale; the higher 108–124 photoelectrons/MeV yield is an estimate for changed fiber collection and sensor configurations, not a measured result from this setup.

sections.title: A hierarchy of exact lower bounds on the Laughlin spectral gap
sections.abstract: The authors combine analytic bounds with finite semidefinite programs to derive lower bounds for the first Haldane pseudopotential's Laughlin gap, including a thermodynamic-limit argument.
sections.claimed_result: The authors present a cutoff-sized SDP whose dependence on flux is parametric, plus an algorithm to produce nearly optimal exact feasible points and certify rank stability in the thermodynamic limit.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated target is the first Haldane pseudopotential on the sphere; extension to Moore–Read and Read–Rezayi pseudopotentials is described as possible, not established here.

sections.title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
sections.abstract: The authors develop a convex-optimization framework for Gaussian-restricted entanglement measures and use it to bound two-way assisted quantum and private communication under input-energy constraints.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive additive Gaussian-restricted entanglement quantities, prove a geometric convergence rate, and obtain communication bounds that match pure-loss benchmarks in selected two- and three-mode examples.
sections.unique_caveat: Gaussian-restricted entanglement quantities need not equal unrestricted ones; the authors treat the latter separately through a photon-number truncation method with controlled error.
